# openinfra_vpc (Resource)

An isolated tenant network domain (kube-ovn) — the AWS VPC. Subnets in different VPCs are fully isolated. Requires the kube-ovn CNI.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Resource name. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `namespace` (String) Kubernetes namespace. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `namespaces` (List of String) Namespaces bound to this VPC (their default subnet lives here).
- `peerings` (Attributes List) VPC peerings — a /30 interconnect to another kind: Vpc (declare on both, plus a route each). Non-transitive, like AWS. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--peerings))
- `routes` (Attributes List) The VPC route table, e.g. 0.0.0.0/0 -> a NatGateway internalIp. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `namespace/name`, the import identifier.
- `ready` (Boolean) Whether the resource's Ready condition is True. Terraform returns as soon as the object is accepted, so this is usually `false` immediately after apply — the platform reconciles asynchronously.

<a id="nestedatt--peerings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `peerings`

Required:

- `local_connect_ip` (String) This VPC's IP on the /30 link, e.g. 169.254.100.1/30.
- `remote_vpc` (String) The kind: Vpc on the other end.


<a id="nestedatt--routes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes`

Required:

- `cidr` (String) Destination CIDR, e.g. 0.0.0.0/0.
- `next_hop` (String) Next-hop IP (a NatGateway internalIp, or a peer-link far side).
